rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration with strong image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and standard RNA encoder (pca_n2000), using weighted fusion. This isolates the impact of encoder choices and fusion method, providing foundational performance data to guide future decisions.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, weighted fusion) achieves 0.5318 accuracy. Uncertainty remains about the impact of image encoder choice (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) on performance. This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 improves accuracy while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of the image encoder. It balances exploration of critical design choices with minimal changes, providing direct evidence about a key component.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with weighted fusion can achieve ~0.53 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a major design choice) with avgpool aggregation, which was not tested in previous top models. It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation while using resnet50 (similar to config_007) to maintain image encoder consistency, providing critical insights into whether multiprofile improves performance without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile and multimodal setups with resnet50 and avgpool aggregation perform well (config_010). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) and aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) to isolate their impact. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/multimodal direction with exploration of advanced encoders and aggregation, which could reveal if these changes improve performance without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile and transformer aggregation significantly improve performance (config_024: 0.713 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → scgpt) while keeping resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (same as config_024) improves accuracy. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a key design decision, on performance.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_024) achieves high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA/scvi_n200, image/resnet50, and transformer aggregation unchanged) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of config_024.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → scgpt) and image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve accuracy. This isolates the impact of representation choices, which are critical for multimodal performance, without altering other key components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (both more complex than pca_n2000/resnet50) with weighted fusion can improve performance, isolating the impact of encoder choices. It balances exploration of complex models against the strong evidence from config_024.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs. scvi_n200 and weighted fusion) could yield comparable performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder and fusion method. It balances exploration of critical design choices while building on prior success with transformer aggregation.

Existing evidence shows that config_024 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). Testing config_032 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping other parameters constant. This clarifies whether pca_n2000 is as effective as scvi_n200 in this setup, a critical design decision with high uncertainty.
